text:
Midday in Burlington and we're sitting at 55 under a gray sky, a few degrees milder than this morning. Clouds hang around through the afternoon, and I'd bet on upper 50s to near 60 for the high before the cold front slips through. Dry air in the low levels should keep any rain out of the lowlands, so at most you'll catch a sprinkle. Nothing you'd need an umbrella for. Sunset is 5:50, and the evening turns clearer and noticeably cooler, with a breeze picking up out of the north after dark.

Tonight we drop to around 31, so the first frost on the windshield is likely by morning. Tuesday is the cold one, sunny but only in the mid 40s with a steady north breeze, so grab the heavier coat. Tuesday night is the coldest of the stretch, around 25 in town, and some spots could even set a record Wednesday morning. It's a short-lived chill, though. We're back to the low 50s Wednesday and near 60 on Thursday.

If you have outdoor errands today, do them this afternoon while it's mild.
